department: Division of Basic Science — Basic Biomedical Sciences (BBS) Umbrella Ph.D. (including Neuroscience)

deadline.value: Online application and all supporting materials (including three letters of recommendation and English proficiency score reports) are due December 1 at 11:59 p.m. CST for fall entry.
deadline.quote: The online application and all supporting materials, including three letters of recommendation, must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. Central Standard Time, Dec. 1.

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for biomedical sciences or neuroscience, and GRE scores are not required for DBS Ph.D. programs.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants do not need to contact professors prior to applying; admitted BBS students complete at least two first-year lab rotations before choosing a dissertation mentor and individual Ph.D. program.
supervisor.quote: It is not necessary for you to contact the professor you are interested in. Contacting them will not have an impact on your application.

also.quote: They also rotate through at least two labs as they narrow down their research interests and potential faculty mentors. Toward the end of the first year, students choose a lab and PhD program to join.

funding.value: All admitted Division of Basic Science Ph.D. students in good academic standing receive guaranteed funding, including a $40,000/year stipend plus full payment of tuition, student service fees, and student health insurance.
funding.quote: Yes, as long as a student is in good academic standing, funding is guaranteed. All students enrolled in the 10 basic science programs receive a nationally competitive stipend of $40,000 per year and tuition, student service fees, and health insurance are paid by the institution.

entry_route.value: Applicants with a U.S. bachelor's degree or equivalent foreign university training (or currently completing a bachelor's degree) are eligible to apply.
entry_route.quote: A bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution of higher learning in the United States or proof of equivalent training at a foreign university is required. Students who are in the process of completing a bachelor's degree are eligible to apply.

notes: Prospective students interested in Neuroscience, Cell and Molecular Biology, Biological Chemistry, Cancer Biology, Genetics Development and Disease, Immunology, Molecular Biophysics, or Molecular Microbiology apply through the single Basic Biomedical Sciences (BBS) umbrella application and join their chosen Ph.D. program toward the end of Year 1.
